National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
1253 AM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The Aviation discussion was updated for the 06Z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. A robust low pressure system will impact the region through
Thanksgiving Day, with frequent wind gusts strong enough to bring
down temporary outdoor structures such as tents and holiday
decorations, and produce isolated power outages. Widespread
rainfall is expected through the morning hours.
2. Gusty winds redevelop this afternoon and continue into Friday
night. Light wintry precipitation is possible near the Tennessee
border tonight into Friday with no significant accumulation. Warmer
for the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: A robust low pressure system will impact the region 
through Thanksgiving Day, with frequent wind gusts strong enough to 
bring down temporary outdoor structures such as tents and holiday 
decorations, and produce isolated power outages. Widespread rainfall 
is expected through the morning hours. 

The overall forecast scenario remains largely on track, with a 
strong low pressure system expected to deepen and move northward 
along the Gulf Stream overnight and then northward across central NC 
this morning into this afternoon. Already we have observed frequent 
wind gusts up to 40 mph from the northeast flow underneath a cold 
air damming wedge firmly entrenched east of the mtns. Thus, the wind 
advisory seems to be working out as designed. While gusts probably 
won't be any stronger than 45 mph away from the highest mountain 
peaks, the Advisory will remain in place because of the potential 
for significant impacts. A few power outages could result and gusts 
will be capable of blowing over holiday decorations, tents, portable 
canopies, etc, many of which are only rated for 25 mph gusts. Be 
prepared for wind gusts to turn over outdoor cooking appliances; 
have a fire extinguisher handy. As the sfc low tracks east of the 
Piedmont this morning, the pressure gradient relaxes temporarily to 
allow gusts to drop off substantially. Wind will increase again, 
though, becoming gusty by this afternoon. 

Meanwhile, the leading edge of the precip continues to push W/NW 
over the forecast area this morning. Temps will remain warm enough 
for all rain. We remain in a Marginal Risk for excessive rain, but 
the likelihood of significant rain across our region has trended 
downward. Unless the low track shifts back to the west, the flood 
risk appears low. Some localized poor drainage flooding could still 
occur, mainly along/E of I-77, if storm drains get clogged by leaves.


Key message 2: Gusty winds redevelop this afternoon and continue 
into Friday night. Light wintry precipitation is possible near the 
Tennessee border tonight into Friday with no significant 
accumulation. Warmer for the weekend.

With the sfc low pulling away to the north this afternoon, the 
pressure gradient will return but with southwest wind aloft that 
will mix down easily underneath a subsidence inversion, though not 
as strong as what we expect through tonight. Gusts are expected to 
be frequent through Thursday night with strong cold advection and 
should persist through Friday until sunset or thereabouts, but the 
potential looks like it will top out in the 25 to 35 mph range at 
best, thus sub-advisory. Unless new guidance comes in, an extension 
of the current Advisory or the issuance of a new one is not planned. 
As to the precip, colder air aloft associated with the upper low 
moving northeast up the TN valley will allow a changeover from rain 
to snow showers with the expected wrap-around precip along the TN 
border Thursday evening. The movement of the upper low, pulling out 
more to the north than usual, will keep the low level flow more W or 
WSW, which is less-than-favorable for upslope forcing away from 
parts of the Smokies, which is a limiting factor. All together, the 
potential for snow accum looks to be an inch or less near the TN 
border. Places east of the spine would most likely remain dry. Temps 
will be cool and on the order of ten degrees below normal on Friday, 
making it feel more like a typical winter day.

The rest of the period looks relatively benign. The upper flow
goes nearly zonal across the South by Saturday with sfc high
pressure moving over the Southeast, which supports a nice warmup
back to normal. A strong shortwave is expected to move out across
the Plains Saturday night and Sunday which will develop another
strong sfc low moving northeastward across the Midwest and lower
Great Lakes Sunday into Monday morning, well to our northwest. This
system should push a cold front across our region Sunday night or
early Monday, but the front will be running out of moisture as it
moves east. While there is some potential for moisture return from
the Gulf ahead of the front, thus perhaps higher precip probs than
some of the guidance would suggest, it is likely that amounts will
be under a quarter inch across all but southwest NC. The flow goes
zonal again behind this system, so more temps near normal can be
expected from Monday onward.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: LLWS remains a concern at KAVL and KHKY 
through 10Z but elsewhere LLWS should remain above 3000 ft AGL. Very 
gusty NE winds will continue through daybreak before a brief lull in 
gusts develops late this morning into early this afternoon. Winds 
turn SW this afternoon while becoming gusty again with gusts 
lingering into tonight. Gusts will mostly range from 20-30+ kts 
through the period outside of the brief lull. IFR to MVFR cig and 
vsby restrictions are noted across the terminals this morning as is -
RA. IFR cigs becoming more widespread through daybreak and should 
stick around through early this evening. -RA will stick around 
through at least daybreak, possibly lingering through mid-morning 
east of the mountains. KAVL should see -RA linger through at least 
the late morning hours. MVFR to IFR vsbys will stick around most of 
the day before lifting to VFR levels late afternoon/early evening. 
Cigs may lift to MVFR towards the end of the period but confidence 
is low so maintained IFR through the end of the 06Z TAF period for 
now. Will reevaluate this for the 12Z TAFs. 

Outlook: A pesky low VFR to high-end MVFR stratocu deck may linger 
into Friday. Gusty west to southwest winds will also linger into 
Friday night. Dry and VFR returns briefly on Saturday before a cold 
front brings a brief shot of rain and associated restrictions Sunday 
afternoon into Sunday night.
